# Part 3 source records: gap sweep (ten gaps named by the critics, and promoted works)

**Date:** 2026-09-29 · generated by `tools/evidence-check/build_part3_files.py` from the verified store; not edited by hand.

Each work was saved as full text and read by one agent, which locked every item to a line of the saved text with a short verbatim anchor. A script checked that each anchor occurs in the saved text and that the numbers of the item stand within three lines of it. A second agent, which did not write the record, then tried to refute each item against the text. Items shown here passed both checks. Where the auditor corrected an item, the corrected wording is shown and the Audit column says so. The verbatim anchors and the saved texts are kept outside the repository; this file gives the location of every item instead. Only works that are eligible under the source rule of 2026-09-29 (D313) are listed; the others are in the evidence ledger, section 1b.

Columns: # = item index (the reference is <record id>#<index>); Field = what the item is about; Line = line in the saved text of the version read. Full references: evidence ledger, References.

| 0 | mechanism | Each round evolves two harness variants in parallel on disjoint component groups; the higher-Pass@1 variant is the winner and its harness is the base of a three-step merge, R3: Revision keeps only loser edits that are independently beneficial and neither duplicate nor conflict with the winner; Recombination applies them with the winner taking precedence on file-level conflicts; Refinement removes redundant edits that implement overlapping functionality. | - | Method description; no measurement. | Sec. HarnessCompass > Component-wise Optimization > Merging the tracks - R3 | 224 | primary | supported |
| 1 | what_is_changed | The harness (base model fixed) has seven component types in two groups: structural (tool implementations, middleware, sub-agent configurations that execute code) and guidance (system prompt, tool descriptions, skills, memory). The loop edits these; the R3 prompt forbids modifying LLM config, tracer, verifier or infrastructure (line 1053). | - | Method description; no measurement. | Sec. HarnessCompass > Preliminaries | 189 | primary | supported |
| 2 | signal | A verifier assigns a binary outcome to each trajectory (1 = task solved); performance is Pass@1, the mean binary success rate over k rollouts per task. The paper does not describe how the verifier decides success. Trajectory evidence and trajectory-grounded first-person feedback inform the meta agent but are not the acceptance signal. | - | Definition of the outcome signal r(tau) in {0,1} (line 189) and Pass@1 (lines 189, 232); verifier mechanism not described in the paper; no measurement. | Sec. HarnessCompass > Preliminaries | 189 | primary | corrected by the auditor |
| 3 | proposal_method | Candidate edits are written by two meta agents (GPT-5.4) running in parallel on the same evidence, differing only in an appended constraint: the structural variant may edit only middleware, tool code and sub-agents (deterministic code, no advisory text); the guidance variant only system prompt, skills, tool descriptions and long-term memory. A generalization gate in the meta agent's system prompt bans task ids, test names, task-under-test symbols and keyword-matching code, and requires each principle to carry an applicability criterion. | - | Method description (Appendix A prompts reproduced verbatim); no measurement. | Appendix A > Component-wise Optimization > Track constraints | 857 | primary | supported |
| 4 | selection_rule | Both track variants are evaluated and the one with the higher Pass@1 on the search tasks is the winner; Algorithm 1 then builds H_t = R3(winner, loser) and accepts it only if the winner's Pass@1 exceeds the current harness's Pass@1 (line 177). The R3 prompt tells the integrator to DROP any loser change it cannot tell helped (line 1003-1005). | - | Selection rule; Pass@1 on the 50-task evolution set; no measurement. | Sec. Component-wise Optimization > Running the tracks independently; Algorithm 1 lines 12-15 | 222 | primary | supported |
| 5 | human_in_loop | All roles in the loop are the same model: code agent, trajectory analyzer, feedback agent and meta agent all run GPT-5.4 in non-thinking mode. Experiments > Setup > Models | 234 | primary | supported |

| # | Field | Claim | Figure | Measurement definition | Location | Line | Label | Audit |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0 | mechanism | ClawTrace registers eight event hooks covering every LLM call, tool use and sub-agent spawn, links child sessions to parent spans, bills cached tokens at their actual rate, and compiles each session into a TraceCard: a ~1.5 kB YAML summary with per-step USD cost, typed token counts, redundant tool-call clusters and failed-or-repaired steps. | ~1.5 kB | Size of one TraceCard (YAML summary of one agent session); Sec. 3.2 gives the typical range as 1.2 to 1.8 kB. Plugin ships for OpenClaw only; other harnesses not validated end-to-end. | Sec. 1 Introduction (contribution 1) | 111 | primary | supported |
| 1 | what_is_changed | The only artifact CostCraft changes is the skill document: all patches are merged into one skill with five sections (Trigger, Workflow, Stop rules, Artifact checklist, Cost control); model weights are not touched (frozen-model, training-free adaptation). | - | Structure of the merged SKILL.md produced by Stage 3 (LLM-based hierarchical merge). | Sec. 3.3 Conflict-aware merge | 167 | primary | supported |
| 2 | proposal_method | Candidate changes are skill patches written by LLM analysts per training trajectory: the Success Analyst reads a successful trajectory's TraceCard and writes up to two patches (one preserve, optionally one prune that targets an expensive step); a prune patch is admitted only if it names a top_cost_spans entry, gives a natural-language counterfactual and is phrased as something to avoid rather than a hard cost cap. | - | Per successful trajectory: at most 1 preserve + 1 prune patch. Failed/partial trajectories go to the Error Analyst (repair patches, Sec. 3.3). | Sec. 3.3 Success Analyst | 163 | primary | supported |
| 3 | selection_rule | Patches are kept or dropped in an LLM-based hierarchical merge with a fixed priority: repair patches with causal diagnosis first, then prune patches with a named cost target and counterfactual, then preserve patches seen in two or more trajectories; singleton preserve patches are dropped; on conflict repair supersedes prune, which supersedes preserve; post-checks enforce the section headings, a 1200-token ceiling and no task-specific leakage. | - | Merge rule of Stage 3; no run-based acceptance test of patches is described in this paragraph. | Sec. 3.3 Conflict-aware merge | 167 | primary | supported |
| 4 | signal | Repair patches are grounded in oracle ground truth: the Error Analyst runs a multi-turn ReAct loop with inspect_mismatches (which rubric items failed), read_gold_snippet (the expected answer) and final_patch, with a budget of 3 lookups; oracle access exists only during offline skill authoring, and preserve and prune patches need no oracle because they are mined from successful trajectories. | - | Supervision used during distillation. Success/failure of a trajectory comes from the benchmark grader (SpreadsheetBench: Q = fraction of rubric items satisfied, Sec. 4.1). | Sec. 3.3 Error Analyst | 165 | primary | supported |
| 5 | result | On the SpreadsheetBench held-out set, removing prune patches (No-prune) tripled regressions at seed 0 from 4 to 13 with comparable median cost, and stripping cost from TraceCards (No-cost-attribution) raised the median cost uplift on successful tasks from +22% to +49% and regressions from 4 to 6; pooled over two seeds Full CostCraft vs No-prune is 5 vs 14 regressions (2.8x). | 4 -> 13 regressions (No-prune, seed 0); 4 -> 6 regressions and +22% -> +49% median cost uplift (No-cost-attribution); pooled 5 vs 14 (2.8x) | 30 held-out SpreadsheetBench tasks, OpenClaw + openai-codex/gpt-5.4; each task compared with its own no-skill baseline at the same seed; regression = Q_skill < Q_baseline - 0.01 (Q = fraction of rubric items satisfied); cost = cache-aware USD per task (per attempt), median uplift over successful tasks. No-cost-attribution is single-seed (N=30, Fig. 3 caption); No-prune seed 1 is 3 vs 5. The text reports No-prune median cost as '+15% vs. +21%' without saying which figure belongs to which condition. | Sec. 4.2 Main Results | 246 | primary | supported |
| 6 | result | Transferred to the full 84-task SkillsBench, the SpreadsheetBench-trained CostCraft skill saves no aggregate cost; all three quality regressions trace to the preserve lane and both quality wins to the prune lane. | 84 tasks | SkillsBench, baseline gpt-5.4 with no skill vs baseline + CostCraft skill; binary Docker pytest verifier; 4 tasks failed at the container layer, leaving 82 cost-paired tasks, 74 quality-gradeable pairs and 79 paired-direction tasks (Sec. 4.5). Aggregate = median per-task cost, $0.143 baseline vs $0.144 CostCraft (Sec. 4.5); lane attribution made by inspection of the merged skill (Sec. 4.5), no SkillsBench ablation run. Seed count for SkillsBench not stated. | Abstract; Sec. 4.5, Table 4 | 101 | primary | supported |
| 7 | loop_cost | The distillation is a single pass, not an iterated loop. 50 SpreadsheetBench tasks are run without a skill, and 10 of them form the evolve set. CostCraft is run once on those 10 TraceCards to produce one skill, and that step is repeated once per ablation condition (Table 3). The held-out tasks are then run under each skill: all 30 tasks for Full CostCraft, No-prune and No-cost-attribution, and a 15-task success-heavy subset for No-CF. | 50 baseline runs; 10 evolve-set TraceCards -> 1 skill; 30 held-out tasks | Evolve set = 4 successes, 4 partial successes, 2 failures; 10 further tasks reserved for pipeline development (Sec. 4.1). Evaluation runs: Full CostCraft and No-prune at two seeds (30 tasks x 2 = 60 runs each; Sec. 5, Table 6). No-cost-attribution uses a single seed (N=30) and No-CF a single seed (N=15) (Fig. 3 caption; Sec. 4.4). Each held-out task is compared with its own no-skill baseline at the same seed; the number of seed-1 baseline runs is not stated separately. Tokens, dollars and wall-clock of the analyst and merge LLM calls themselves are not reported, and the analyst LLM is not named. | Sec. 4.1 Setup | 241 | primary | corrected by the auditor |
| 8 | limitation | All claims are scoped to one runtime and backbone (OpenClaw with openai-codex/gpt-5.4); within-seed cost CV is near 43%; the No-prune Q=0 severity is seed-0-specific; the failure taxonomy was coded by one annotator; two heuristic TraceCard fields were not exercised because no sub-agents were spawned. | - | Authors' own limitations section; also: 30 held-out tasks at two seeds (60 runs per condition), 74 of 84 SkillsBench pairs gradeable; Sec. 5 second paragraph adds that two prune rules match only 2 of 17 successful held-out tasks and no SkillsBench ablation matrix was run. | Sec. 5 Limitations | 299 | primary | supported |
| 9 | human_in_loop | The authors list a closed loop that feeds trace-derived findings back into skill updates without manual intervention among the upcoming (not yet available) features of the ClawTrace platform. | - | Platform roadmap statement in the appendix demo section; the paper describes no human review step inside CostCraft, and the Table 2 failure taxonomy was hand-coded by one annotator (Sec. 3.4, Sec. 5). | Appendix A ClawTrace Platform Demo | 502 | primary | supported |
